Subject: High error rate and throughput drop on our Private cluster (HarborCare-prod)

Hi Olga / Marissa,

We're seeing a sharp increase in 500/503 responses and a ~4x p95 latency regression starting ~15:50 PDT on our private VPC cluster (HarborCare-prod). This affects both synchronous inference and a nightly batch that runs short sequences (~400 tokens) — we've started seeing timeouts and retries that are spiking downstream errors.

We opened a ticket with your support and attached a short p99 trace; DevOps are available if you need SSH access. We need help diagnosing root cause and an ops plan ASAP — Rajiv is looped in.

Attachments: harborcare_p99_trace.log

Thanks,
Aisha
Head of Product Operations
HarborCare

Subject: Re: High error rate and throughput drop on our Private cluster (HarborCare-prod)

Hi Aisha — thanks for the heads-up and for the trace. We're treating this as a priority incident.

Immediate plan:
- I'll stand up a 30‑minute war room at 17:00 PDT to triage (invite shortly).
- Technical triage: Vivek will start looking at runtime logs and KV cache eviction patterns; Rishi will review kernel/driver errors in the node logs.
- If we confirm a capacity or kvcache regression, we will propose a safe rollback or a constrained routing rule to divert short critical requests to a low-latency pool.

Please share SSH access to one of the affected jump hosts and the deploy manifest (harborcare_deploy_manifest.yaml) if possible. We may ask for temporary elevated telemetry retention.

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>; marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>; rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High error rate and throughput drop on our Private cluster (HarborCare-prod) — initial findings

War room notes (first pass):
- Observed symptom: p95 latency jumped from ~220ms to ~950ms; 503/504s cluster-wide but concentrated on two worker nodes.
- Promising lead: KV cache churn correlates with the start of a customer ETL job at 15:48 PDT. Trace shows repeated full-cache rehydration and >40% eviction rate during the spike.
- Node errors: repeated GPU driver preemption messages and transient OOMs on the same two nodes; OS level shows GPU memory fragmentation metrics increasing before OOM.
- Hypothesis: A burst of concurrent short-sequence jobs overwhelmed the batching heuristics and caused small batches to be repeatedly scheduled, thrashing KV cache and triggering driver preemption on older GPU drivers. That sequence causes elevated tail latency and retries that cascade into higher load.

Immediate mitigations we recommend now (safe, non-disruptive):
1) Apply a temporary route rule on HarborCare-prod to limit concurrent batch window for the nightly ETL (reduce concurrency from 64 -> 12) and mark those jobs as low-priority.
2) Increase kvcache.size by 20% on the two affected worker groups to reduce eviction; this is a config change in the runtime and is hot-reloadable for the most part.
3) Lower max_batch_latency for short-sequence routes (reduces batch packing delays that are creating jitter).

If mitigations look good, we'll schedule a rolling patch for the driver/kernel and coordinate a small restart window for the two nodes (safe, staggered).

Attaching: kvcache_eviction_flamegraph.svg (summary), harborcare_p99_trace.log (from Aisha).

— Vivek
Principal SWE, Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@harborcare.health>
To: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Khatri <aisha.khatri@harborcare.health>, devops@harborcare.health
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 18:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High error rate and throughput drop on our Private cluster (HarborCare-prod) — leadership note

Olga / Marissa,

Thanks for the quick triage. We are seeing user-impacting failures across three downstream services (billing, notifications, and triage ingestion). I need a concise mitigation timeline and confirmation we won't trigger a larger outage when you perform the suggested restarts.

We need answers to:
- Expected customer-visible recovery time for the temporary routing + kvcache change?
- If driver/kernel patch is required, can it be limited to the two nodes only and done in a staggered fashion?
- Do you recommend short-term credits or an SLA exception while we stabilize?

Rajiv
CTO, HarborCare
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@harborcare.health>; Aisha Khatri <aisha.khatri@harborcare.health>; vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>; rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, devops@harborcare.health
Date: Sat, 21 Jul 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High error rate and throughput drop on our Private cluster (HarborCare-prod) — proposed ops plan and exec asks

Rajiv — quick answers and concrete plan: 
- Recovery expectation: The routing rule + kvcache increase should reduce p95 back to ~300–350ms and cut 503s by ~70% within the first 15–30 minutes after application. We'll monitor and report at 15-minute intervals.
- Rolling patch window: Yes — we propose a 3-step staggered restart limited to the two problematic worker groups (max 1 node offline at a time); estimated impact: ephemeral queueing for < 2m per node during connection handover. We'll only proceed with your approval.
- Credits/SLA: Our accounts team is prepared to discuss a pro-rated credit for the affected billing period. I'll loop in Finance if you want to start that dialogue immediately.

Immediate actions (next 90 minutes):
1) Apply routing rule to constrain nightly ETL concurrency. (Ops: HarborCare DevOps + Redwood runtime policy).
2) Hot-increase kvcache.size by 20% on affected groups. (Runtime config change, no reboot).
3) Short telemetry window: extend trace retention to 48h for deeper RCA.
4) If metrics don't improve within 45 minutes, schedule a staggered rolling restart and driver update for the two nodes (weekend low-traffic window if you prefer).

Request from HarborCare: please confirm SSH access details for one jump host and permission to run a controlled restart if needed.

I'll run the post-incident summary and RCA within 72 hours and include actionable tunings (batch heuristics, kvcache sizing rules, and a recommended driver bump cadence).

— Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
